title: Two edits, one batch
intro: Five filings, one fixed extraction prompt, two failures. One engineer edits the instruction string; the other edits the assembly step. Both diffs are small. Only one of them moves the pass rate — and the last step shows the same reflex applied where it loses money.

provenance.source: a narrated five-filing extraction batch under two competing edits; token counts and prices are plausible inventions, not measurements

foot: This walks M02's Where Prompt-Only Breaks — grounding, memory, tools, governance — and then its counterweight, layer maximalism.

steps.title: The batch, and which layer each failure is missing
narrative: One prompt — extract the debtor name as JSON — run across five filings. Three pass. The UCC-3 amendment invents a debtor because the original filing it points at was never retrieved. The redacted filing returns a different JSON shape on every run.
Classify the failures by what is absent, not by what the prompt says. Amendment: no grounding. Redacted: no governance. Neither cell in that table has a wording fix in it.
steps.youDo: Run your own fixed prompt over a batch that includes your ugliest inputs, and label each failure grounding / memory / tool / governance before you touch the prompt.

steps.title: Edit A — work the sentence
narrative: The first engineer opens the prompt file. Role added, emphasis added, an explicit rule about amendments added. It is a careful edit and it reads better than what it replaced.

It moves 34 tokens. Re-run the batch: still 3/5. The amendment case now knows that the name may live in an original filing, and still cannot reach it. Telling a model about a document is not the same as putting the document in the window.
steps.claudeSays: The new rule told me where the name lives. I have no way to open that filing from here, so I filled the field the only way left.

view.question: extract the debtor name from 2024-FL-0024117
view.verdictNote: 3/5, unchanged — 34 tokens of better wording against a missing document

steps.title: Edit B — work the assembly
narrative: The second engineer never opens the prompt file. PROMPT_V1 ships unchanged. The edit is four lines in the assembly step: if the filing is a UCC-3 and names an original, fetch it and put it in the window under its own heading.

That moves 1,180 tokens — the retrieved original filing — and the amendment resolves to ACME LOGISTICS & DISTRIBUTION, L.L.C. with a citation. A JSON-schema constraint on the same call fixes the redacted case. 5/5, at 3,360 tokens and just over a cent.
steps.claudeSays: The name came out of the retrieved original. Nothing about how I was asked changed between the failing run and this one.
steps.youDo: Diff the two edits by the question "how many tokens did this move?" A prompt rewrite moves tens. An assembly change moves thousands. Leverage follows the tokens.

steps.title: Two diffs, and the edit that goes the wrong way
narrative: Side by side: 34 tokens for no change in pass rate, 1,180 tokens for +2. That ratio is the paradigm shift in one number, and it is why the discipline renamed itself.

Now the inverse mistake, because it is the same reflex pointed at the wrong problem. The help button answers "what is a UCC-1?" from a 90-token prompt, correctly, every time. Someone adds retrieval, tool defs and session memory "to be safe": 4,130 input tokens for the identical sentence back — 46x the input for zero reliability gain, on a task that was never missing a layer.
Both halves are the same skill. Ask which layer is missing; add exactly that one; and when the honest answer is none, ship the prompt.
steps.youDo: For every layer in your current pipeline, name the failure it prevents. Any layer you cannot attach a failure to is dilution you are paying for.

items.label: edit B — retrieve the referenced filing

views.text: 46x the input tokens and 6.8x the cost to return the same sentence. Layer maximalism is the mirror image of prompt whack-a-mole and it bills you for the privilege. The judgment M02 is teaching is not "add layers" — it is add the missing one, and be able to name it.
